clinician.final_diagnosis: Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) secondary to myelodysplastic syndrome with multilineage dysplasia (MDS-MLD)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old man with MDS-MLD diagnosed 6 years prior presented to dermatology with a 2-year history of severe photosensitivity and crusting skin lesions. Clinical presentation was characterized by burning and excruciating pain in sun-exposed areas (face, hands, fingertips) occurring within 30 minutes of direct sun exposure, with crusting lesions appearing on the dorsal hands within days. Physical examination revealed thickened, lichenified skin with fresh blisters, numerous crusts, indented scars, and milia formation on the dorsal hands, back of neck, and face—findings consistent with EPP. Biochemical confirmation was obtained via plasma fluorescence scan showing massive elevation of total porphyrins (33.9 μmol/L, normal <1.30) and free protoporphyrin (30 μmol/L, normal <0.20). Complete blood count documented anaemia with reduced thrombocytes and white blood cells consistent with his underlying MDS. Liver and renal function were normal, and no autoantibodies associated with connective tissue diseases were detected. The patient was managed with sun-protective measures and did not require afamelanotide. Two years after EPP diagnosis, he maintained good control of photosensitivity with these measures and showed no signs of liver toxicity despite persistently elevated plasma porphyrins on regular monitoring.
